authority: databrowser-meta plans/AUDIT-metadata-reachable-fields.md sections 2 and 3 (the TABLES, never the prose counts), widened by plans/PLAN-define-ct-evaluation.md T1-3 (b) and T1-9 (every field the pickle cache publishes, at every level, except _links and the Python cache builder's additions), and by plans/PLAN-store-cdash-codelist-ids.md (owner 2026-09-28: T1-9's one _links-derived projection, codelistIds from _links.codelist, covers CDASH fields as well as variables - two codelistIds rows, one per level)
purpose: Data only: the argument for every row lives in the audit and the plan and is not repeated here.
This file freezes WHAT the store carries, at every level, with the TYPE of each slot - and,
since format 3, WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CARRY: every level's `excluded` block names each
source key the projection never reads, with its reason, so silence can no longer mean 'dropped'.
It exists because the store had already been silently narrowed twice: `examples` was typed
List<String> against an array-only reader, so the field was dropped from every seeded store while
a fixture-fed round-trip test stayed green (fixed in 948647c, StoreFormat.FORMAT_VERSION 1 -> 2);
and the codelist `name` was the one codelist-level field the source publishes that no manifest row
and no record carried, which no leg could see (fixed by PLAN-define-ct-evaluation, 2 -> 3).
3 -> 4 (PLAN-store-cdash-codelist-ids) is a widening, not a repair: CDASH fields gained the
codelistIds projection the variables already had.

typeVocabulary.nested: record component List<the record of the level named by `element`>

reachedByVocabulary.both: read by coreJ and by the Python engine
reachedByVocabulary.python: read by the Python engine only
reachedByVocabulary.neither: read by neither - stored as future-proofing, and a re-seed cannot be pushed to users retroactively
reachedByVocabulary.none: read by nothing yet - stored under T1-9 (the pickle cache is the universe), for a later need

fieldKeys.source: the key in the source metadata JSON; omitted when identical to `field`
fieldKeys.sourceless: true when no source key feeds it (the store's own identity slots)
fieldKeys.transformed: true when the projection rewrites the value, so it is not equal to its source text
fieldKeys.element: for `nested`: the level the elements belong to

excludedKeys.source: a top-level key the SOURCE publishes at this level that the projection deliberately does not read
excludedKeys.reason: why - T1-9 admits exactly two reasons for a pickle key: it is `_links`, or the Python cache builder added it; an API-only key is recorded for the record
